rows.core: Turn-specific opponent-life-loss threshold powers cascade on hand-cast spells; Solphim and cheap pingers raise the threshold without replacing Abaddon.
rows.positive: Aggravated Assault can create additional attack and main phases; with mana and unblocked attackers, extra opponent life loss may enlarge later Abaddon cascade thresholds.
rows.cut_cost: Mystic Remora is one-blue early card advantage against opponents' noncreature spells; losing it deprives a mid-power cascade deck of efficient fuel and answers while preparing Abaddon.
rules: Abaddon's granted cascade checks spells cast from hand during your turn and the total opponent life lost that turn.
Aggravated Assault activates only at sorcery speed, costs {3}{R}{R}, and untaps creatures plus generates additional combat and main phase.
Additional combat damage may contribute to Abaddon's threshold but does not itself cascade or recur the Assault activation cost.
Mystic Remora taxes noncreature spells at the point opponents cast them and can draw multiple cards before Abaddon is active.
An Assault infinite-combat line requires actual attack-trigger mana creation or other demonstrated mana-positive source, not just a Spellbook completion.
rows.adverse: High recurring activation cost plus extra combat does not automatically increase spells available from hand; the candidate removes the source's best early noncreature-spell draw.
rows.followup: Compare Assault activation turns with source lands/rituals, damage threshold and eligible hand spells against Remora early opponents' turns.

rows.core: Enemy-card theft turns opponents' creatures into enhanced Pirates and opponent-owned noncreature spells into Treasure generation.
rows.positive: Tidespout Tyrant might bounce opposing blockers or permanents during long spell chains, reopening theft attacks without relying on battle damage.
rows.cut_cost: Deadly Rollick is conditional free instant-speed creature exile when a commander is controlled; it can preserve Don Andres or remove the lethal blocker before attack.
rules: Don Andres rewards creatures you control but do not own, and noncreature spells you cast that you do not own.
Casting your own Tidespout Tyrant does not, by itself, satisfy the don't-own spell payoff.
A bounced opposing permanent returns to its owner's hand; ordinary Tyrant bounce does not put its card under your control.
Tidespout needs spells cast after it resolves and their mana costs must be paid for repeat control.
Deadly Rollick alternate cost requires you to control a commander, not merely have one in the command zone.
rows.adverse: Seven-mana generic bounce control replaces free removal without improving the commander's stole-card cast count; tempo and protected theft lines suffer.
rows.followup: Test actual Don Andres captured noncreature spells and Treasure generation before a source-payable Tyrant spell chain, including a blocker response.

rows.core: Artifact-spell cast triggers recover matching copies from graveyard/hand/library through counter and exile stax; colorless activations matter only after artifact access.
rows.positive: The Enigma Jewel cheaply supplies mana for artifact activated abilities; its crafted face could offer copied activated abilities in a longer stax game.
rows.cut_cost: Mox Amber is a zero-mana colored source when Mishra or another qualifying legendary creature/planeswalker is controlled and serves as a low-cost artifact cast under selective stax.
rules: Mishra triggers on artifact spell casting; the matching-name card can be fetched from permitted zones, but the cast itself remains subject to counterspells.
The Enigma Jewel's mana is restricted to costs of activated abilities, not Mishra's triggered retrieval or artifact spell costs.
The Jewel enters tapped and cannot immediately pay its tap ability on entering.
The Jewel is itself an artifact spell and can trigger Mishra, but Commander singleton usually prevents fetching a second same-name card without a separate zone/copy circumstance.
The crafted Locus is not automatically available: source-approved exiled materials and crafting payments must be verified.
rows.adverse: Jewel cannot fund the deck's early stax artifact casts or Mishra's trigger; taking away zero-mana Mox Amber can impair the asymmetry setup.
rows.followup: Identify exact approved artifact activated-ability payments and earliest crafted-face line; compare colored mana/lock deployment when Mox Amber stays.
rows.add: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment

rows.core: Commander grows when any player sacrifices a creature and forces the defender to sacrifice on attack; edicts and sacrifice control clear a commander-damage route.
rows.positive: Relic of Legends adds a mana rock that can tap legendary creatures to produce another colored mana, theoretically allowing postcombat ritual or removal development.
rows.cut_cost: Black Market Connections is repeatable life-for-cards, Treasure and creature generation; the 3/2 changeling body can be edict fodder and draw supplies protected attack turns.
rules: Thraximundar gains +1/+1 counters on any player sacrificing a creature; sacrificing mana rocks is not a creature sacrifice.
Relic of Legends can tap an untapped legendary creature for mana, but a Thraximundar tapped for mana cannot also be declared an attacker that turn without untapping.
Relic's ordinary tap-mana mode is not a free extra legendary activation.
Black Market Connections creates a Treasure, draws or makes a 3/2 Shapeshifter with life payments during precombat main, supplying board and hand separately.
Thraximundar's attack edict alone does not guarantee an opponent sacrifices multiple creatures if board positions make a single forced sacrifice possible.
rows.adverse: Replacing a scalable card/Treasure/fodder engine with a three-mana narrow rock can slow both interaction and forced-sacrifice plan.
rows.followup: Compare early commander casting and subsequent edict count with Connections life budget versus Relic's colored mana across two turns.

rows.core: Commander reanimates exactly Pirate creature cards at each own combat, with finality counters and temporary haste; ETB Pirates plus finality management define the engine.
rows.positive: Tidespout Tyrant might help bounce large permanents while assembling a Pirates attack board, potentially protecting a slower value game.
rows.cut_cost: Deadly Rollick conditionally exiles a blocker or graveyard-reanimator threat at no mana while Admiral Brass is controlled, preserving combat and chosen Pirate target.
rules: Admiral Brass's beginning-of-combat reanimation targets Pirate creature cards, not arbitrary creatures.
Tidespout Tyrant is a Djinn, not a Pirate; it cannot ordinarily be the Admiral's combat reanimation target.
A returned Pirate with a finality counter is exiled instead of dying, limiting standard recursion without counter removal.
Tidespout's cast triggers need post-resolution spells and do not multiply the Admiral's combat trigger by themselves.
Deadly Rollick's free casting condition is controlling a commander; casting it at a contested reanimation window may protect the combat line.
rows.adverse: Tyrant becomes a commander-independent seven/eight-mana threat that costs protected creature removal and is not a Pirate target; historical raw SHA mismatch must not be silently repaired.
rows.followup: Test actual Pirates returned per combat and conditional Rollick protection compared with fully paid Tyrant; reconcile recorded/raw source hashes separately.

rows.core: Sedris grants own graveyard creatures unearth {2}{B}, enabling transient ETB reanimation, repeat with reductions and doubling, and self-mill as fuel.
rows.positive: The Enigma Jewel provides mana usable for the generic portion of unearth activated abilities, potentially sustaining one or more graveyard activations after Sedris is on board.
rows.cut_cost: Jeska's Will generates red mana or playable exiled cards at sorcery speed and can grant both modes with commander controlled, supplying burst mana and castable spells for graveyard turns.
rules: Unearth is an activated ability of creature cards in graveyard and is restricted to sorcery timing; its activation mana may be partly paid with Jewel's restricted mana.
The Jewel only generates colorless ability mana, never the {B} required by Sedris-granted unearth.
Jewel enters tapped, so it cannot activate its tap-mana ability immediately without untapping.
Sedris's unearth replacement exiles a returned permanent if it would leave the battlefield and at end step, making recursion and blink lines timing-sensitive.
Jeska's Will is not an activated ability and cannot be paid with restricted Jewel mana.
rows.adverse: A one-mana tap artifact may help later ability-heavy turns but is slower than red burst mana on the key turn; no source-paid unearth improvement is established.
rows.followup: Trace source graveyard creature count, Jewel generic payments, black pips, end-step timing and Will dual-mode sequences across paired hands.
rows.add: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment
